chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about the ghusl of the two Eids: is it obligatory? He said: It is a sunnah. I said: Then Friday? He said: It is a sunnah. As for what has been narrated that the ghusl of Friday is obligatory and the term obligation has been applied to it, the meaning in that is the emphasis of the sunnah and the intensity of its recommendation, and that is expressed by the term obligation; and among that is:

key_terms.تَأْكِيدُ السُّنَّةِ: the stressing or emphatic affirmation of a sunnah practice
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْعِيدَيْنِ: the ritual bath associated with the two Eid occasions
key_terms.وَاجِبٌ: obligatory; here discussed and clarified as not literal obligation

ai.seo_question: Is the ghusl of Friday and the two Eids obligatory or recommended in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the ghusl for the two Eids and for Friday is sunnah (prophetically recommended), not obligatory. It also explains that reports using the wording of wujub regarding Friday ghusl are understood as emphasizing the sunnah and its strong recommendation.
